network.overall_strategy: Construct an evidence-qualified network containing ten distinct graph or experimental-protocol pathways, not ten independently established histidine-forming mechanisms. P1 is the experimentally supported, precursor-fed Shen synthesis. P2 and P3 are conditional upstream extensions through glycolaldehyde aldol and formose chemistry. P4-P9 represent the six reported reactor/pH configurations of Criado-Reyes et al. (2021); P10 represents Jiang et al. (2014). These seven discharge pathways are empirical source terms, not resolved molecular mechanisms or seven independent reaction families. Erythrose can be supplied initially or generated through the optional upstream reactions; formamidine is a conditional external feedstock because productive geochemical synthesis and persistence are unresolved. All routes use anoxic surface gas-water systems or staged aqueous compartments. Alkaline sugar production, mildly acidic imidazole assembly, cyanide capture, and acidic hydrolysis are not assumed to occur simultaneously in one pond. Proposed operating windows are distinguished from reported experimental parameters, and missing concentrations or residence times are not invented. The 15 K ice experiments are outside the stipulated terrestrial environments; hot dry CO/H2/NH3 catalysis is not relabeled as demonstrated aqueous hydrothermal synthesis. Molecules use neutral reference formulas with pH-dependent protonation omitted. Discharge reactions are atom-balanceable selected-product projections: hydrogen bookkeeping does not establish measured H2 production, and nitrogen provenance remains unresolved. The network is structurally complete for these selected pathways but is not a fully validated end-to-end geochemical synthesis. No enantiomeric enrichment is assumed.

reactions.name: Conditional erythrose supply by glycolaldehyde self-aldol chemistry

conditions.temperature: 300-330 K; proposed screening window, not a reported histidine-network protocol
conditions.other: Proposed pH 9-11 in alkaline, concentrating water. Effective glycolaldehyde concentration, residence time, erythrose yield, and survival time are not established by the supplied research. The selected product node represents the D-erythrose fraction of an expected stereoisomeric mixture, not selective D-erythrose production. Transfer to the imidazole stage requires quenching alkaline chemistry and demonstrating an approximately 30 mM erythrose inventory.

reactions.mechanism: Base-catalyzed enolization and intermolecular aldol addition combine glycolaldehyde units into aldotetroses. Erythrose is one product alongside other stereoisomers and competing products.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative as an integrated feedstock-supply step, although the aldol reaction class is established. Shen et al. (1987) used supplied erythrose rather than demonstrating this upstream production-and-transfer sequence. Vázquez-Salazar et al. (2018) identify tetrose scarcity and instability as major limitations. Neither citation establishes selective, persistent erythrose accumulation under the proposed conditions. This edge therefore cannot inherit the experimental confidence or histidine yield of the downstream Shen synthesis.

reactions.name: Conditional formaldehyde-fed formose branch to erythrose

conditions.other: Proposed pH 10-11 in a calcium-bearing concentrating pool. Glycolaldehyde supplies a C2 entry substrate; formaldehyde supplies additional carbon. Productive feed concentrations and residence time are not established for coupling to histidine synthesis. Terminate alkaline aging before extensive sugar degradation, then change to approximately pH 6. No experimentally demonstrated concentration or selection process delivering 30 mM erythrose is assumed.

reactions.mechanism: A coarse-grained formose branch incorporates C1 units through aldol additions and carbonyl isomerizations to produce a tetrose mixture containing erythrose. It is not an elementary or selective formaldehyde-to-erythrose reaction.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative as a completed upstream connection. Formose chemistry is discussed as a possible erythrose source in the Shen framework, but the supplied studies do not demonstrate crude formose mixture to histidine conversion (Shen et al., 1987; Shen et al., 1990). The instability and low selectivity emphasized by Vázquez-Salazar et al. (2018) remain unresolved. Calcium and hydroxide are included for their established roles in formose chemistry, not as histidine-specific catalysts.

reactions.name: Experimentally supported erythrose-formamidine assembly of imidazole-4-acetaldehyde

conditions.other: Reported precursor experiment: 0.03 M D-erythrose and 0.03 M formamidine, approximately pH 6.0, heated for 12 h. No added mineral catalyst. A terrestrial implementation requires replenishment or transient concentration of both precursors, protection against destructive surface irradiation, and prompt downstream use. The experimental concentrations were 0.03 M, not 0.3 M.

reactions.mechanism: Net condensation, rearrangement, and dehydration assemble the substituted imidazole ring. An Amadori-like sequence is proposed; the exact microscopic order is not established. Water is the formal condensation coproduct.
reactions.reasoning: Directly supported precursor chemistry: Shen et al. (1987) identified imidazole-4-acetaldehyde and reported a maximum yield of 1.6% relative to erythrose. Shen et al. (1990) subsequently obtained histidine after adding HCN and ammonia to the precursor-generating mixture. The aldehyde maximum and the later 3.5% histidine yield are different experimental observations and must not be multiplied as isolated sequential yields. Formamidine hydrolysis and erythrose decay remain central geochemical bottlenecks (Vázquez-Salazar et al., 2018). No productive formamidine-supply reaction is invented here.

reactions.name: Strecker capture of imidazole-4-acetaldehyde

conditions.temperature: 300-330 K; proposed capture window, not a recovered Shen experimental value
conditions.pressure: Near ambient, with gas-liquid retention or replenishment
conditions.other: Proposed staging at approximately pH 8-9 after the aldehyde-generating stage. HCN and ammonia must be retained or replenished because volatilization competes with capture. Their experimental concentrations and reaction duration are not supplied in the research summary and are not assigned invented values. Rock-covered aqueous compartments could attenuate surface UV but have not been experimentally coupled to this synthesis.

reactions.mechanism: Ammonia forms an imine or iminium equivalent with the aldehyde; cyanide addition installs the alpha-amino nitrile center. The imine is treated as a transient mechanistic species rather than a separately established accumulated intermediate.
reactions.reasoning: This is a mechanistic subdivision of the experimentally completed Strecker sequence reported by Shen et al. (1990), not an independently demonstrated isolation of the aminonitrile. Their multi-technique identification of histidine supports the overall aldehyde-mixture plus HCN/ammonia connection. The supplied research does not establish the proposed capture window, productive reagent ratios, residence time, or physical coupling to a natural pool; those remain validation requirements.

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of histidine aminonitrile to histidine

conditions.temperature: 350-370 K; proposed hydrolysis window, not a reported validated residence-time regime
conditions.other: Proposed separate acidic stage at approximately pH 1-2 after cyanide capture. Residual cyanide management and precursor survival must be established before acidification. The supplied Shen summary does not provide hydrolysis temperature, acidity, or duration, so no numerical residence time is claimed. Histidine and released ammonia are predominantly protonated under these conditions; neutral formulas are bookkeeping references.

reactions.mechanism: Nitrile hydration followed by amide hydrolysis produces the carboxylic acid and releases the nitrile nitrogen as ammonia/ammonium. The transient amide is not asserted to have been isolated.
reactions.reasoning: Conventional hydrolysis closes the Strecker interpretation of the histidine synthesis demonstrated by Shen et al. (1990), whose overall histidine yield was 3.5% relative to erythrose. That endpoint does not independently validate this proposed mild-temperature acidic implementation. Hydrolysis rate, competing decomposition, and the attainable yield require measurement. Avoiding the hottest hydrothermal regimes is justified by the general amino-acid destruction observed by Ito et al. (2006), but those measurements are not histidine-specific rate constants.

reactions.name: Empirical histidine source: buffered discharge in a Teflon-only reactor

conditions.temperature: 300-370 K receiving-water scenario; exact experimental reservoir temperature is not specified in the supplied report; spark plasma is nonthermal
conditions.pressure: Reported initial partial pressures: CH4 200 ± 20 mbar, NH3 200 ± 20 mbar, N2 100 ± 20 mbar; water vapor additional
conditions.other: Reported protocol: 200 mL water, approximately 30 kV discharge, 14 days elapsed with approximately seven days energized; approximately pH 8.7 with 0.05 M NH4Cl. Teflon-only reactor without borosilicate. Teflon is an experimental inert-wall control, not a proposed natural mineral. No added H2 or O2.

reactions.mechanism: Unresolved gas-phase and aqueous organic chemistry followed by analytical recovery of a histidine-assigned product. No erythrose, imidazole aldehyde, Strecker, or hydantoin mechanism is assigned.
reactions.reasoning: Criado-Reyes et al. (2021) reported histidine in the buffered Teflon-only configuration, showing that borosilicate is not obligatory. Buffered configurations collectively yielded approximately 0.08-0.12 mg histidine per experiment; the supplied summary does not assign a specific value to this configuration. Identification used derivatized GC-MS library matching, and histidine was not among the explicitly co-injected authentic-standard confirmations. This is an empirical source term, not an elementary reaction. N2 is retained on both sides without asserting nitrogen provenance; H2 enables formal selected-product bookkeeping and is not a reported stoichiometric yield.

reactions.mechanism: Empirical, unresolved discharge-driven formation and aqueous processing of a complex organic mixture containing the histidine-assigned endpoint.
reactions.reasoning: Histidine was reported in this configuration by Criado-Reyes et al. (2021). Glass affected the broader product network, but the paper does not establish a glass-catalyzed histidine mechanism. The approximately 0.08-0.12 mg range applies across buffered configurations, not a known configuration-specific value here. The GC-MS assignment and absence of target-specific co-injection require qualification. This is a reactor-surface variant of rxn_006, not independent evidence for a second molecular mechanism; gas coproduct bookkeeping is not a measured product balance.

reactions.name: Empirical histidine source: seven-day methane-ammonia-hydrogen discharge

conditions.temperature: 353 K water reservoir; discharge zone is nonthermal
conditions.pressure: Near ambient gas-balloon apparatus; exact partial pressures not provided in the supplied summary

The three-day experiment is not counted as an independently demonstrated histidine pathway.

reactions.mechanism: Unresolved discharge-driven carbon and nitrogen chemistry followed by aqueous accumulation and amino-acid analysis. Hydrogen appears on both sides because it is a feed gas and a formal redox-balancing pool in this selected-product projection.

Analysis used derivatization and LC-MS/MS against amino-acid standards, but the supplied record gives no absolute histidine yield or target-specific mechanism. Consequently, this source term is not routed through erythrose or imidazole-4-acetaldehyde. Continuous energy input, replenished reduced gases, and laboratory gas retention are important boundary conditions, not demonstrated natural steady states. No measured net H2 yield is implied.

pathways.name: Precursor-fed Shen synthesis
pathways.description: Begin with supplied D-erythrose and formamidine, generate imidazole-4-acetaldehyde, and complete the Strecker sequence. The experimental overall precursor-to-histidine connection is supported; separately represented aminonitrile capture and proposed environmental hydrolysis conditions are not independently validated. External precursor availability remains conditional.

pathways.name: Glycolaldehyde-fed extension of the Shen pathway
pathways.description: Generate an erythrose-containing mixture by glycolaldehyde self-aldol chemistry, then enter the shared Shen sequence. Productive erythrose concentration, selection, preservation, and transfer have not been demonstrated. This is a conditional upstream extension, not an independently validated complete synthesis.

pathways.name: Formaldehyde-fed formose extension of the Shen pathway
pathways.description: Use formaldehyde and glycolaldehyde in an alkaline formose branch, then transfer an erythrose fraction into the shared imidazole and Strecker chemistry. The end-to-end sequence is unvalidated; incompatible reaction stages and sugar instability are explicit bottlenecks.

pathways.name: Hydrogen-containing seven-day discharge protocol
pathways.description: Jiang et al. (2014), methane-ammonia-hydrogen-water discharge with replenished gases. Histidine is included in the reported amino-acid inventory, but no target-specific intermediate sequence or absolute histidine yield is established in the supplied record.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The strongest pathway. Shen et al. (1987, 1990) support imidazole-4-acetaldehyde formation and subsequent histidine production, with 3.5% histidine yield relative to erythrose and multiple analytical identifications. The aminonitrile is a sound mechanistic intermediate, although the supplied evidence does not establish its independent isolation. External precursor feeding is legitimate for this conditional synthesis. Environmental confidence remains limited by precursor persistence, unspecified downstream operating conditions, and the unestablished natural implementation of acidic hydrolysis.
suggestions: Attach the reported rxn_003 conditions: approximately 0.03 M each precursor, pH 6, 80 C, and 12 hours. Do not automatically assign these conditions to rxn_004 or rxn_005.
Document verified Strecker and hydrolysis conditions, distinguishing preparative chemistry from analytical work-up and leaving unavailable parameters explicitly unknown.
Specify physically plausible concentration, retention, and pH-adjustment processes, and assess precursor degradation during those operations.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Glycolaldehyde self-aldol chemistry can supply aldotetroses, making this a plausible upstream extension rather than an established end-to-end histidine synthesis. The unresolved issue is delivery of sufficient surviving erythrose from a mixed product stream into the Shen sequence. No catalyst, operating conditions, erythrose yield, or successful mixture handoff is documented for rxn_001. The D-erythrose label should not imply stereoselective production from achiral feedstocks.
suggestions: Provide experimental support for erythrose production under a specified catalyst, pH, temperature, and residence time, including competing products and degradation.
Represent the upstream erythrose pool without implying enantiomeric enrichment, and test its direct use in the Shen condensation.
Specify the alkaline-to-mildly-acidic handoff and subsequent hydrolysis conditions, including dilution and material losses.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The formaldehyde-fed formose edge is defensible as a selected-product, multistep projection, not as a selective elementary reaction. The literature supports tetrose formation generally but highlights low selectivity and erythrose instability. This network does not establish that its formose mixture supplies the concentrations needed downstream. Glycolaldehyde remains an explicit co-feed, so this is not a demonstrated formaldehyde-only entry route. The conditional designation appropriately limits the claim.
suggestions: Document the formose catalyst and operating conditions, with measured erythrose abundance and stability rather than total sugar yield alone.
Retain glycolaldehyde as an explicit co-feed or independently validate its production; clarify that rxn_002 summarizes a reaction network.
Demonstrate transfer of the actual sugar mixture into imidazole assembly, accounting for stereoisomers, competing carbonyls, dilution, and precursor decay.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Criado-Reyes et al. (2021) support a histidine endpoint in buffered Teflon experiments, so an empirical source term without a mineral requirement is justified. The histidine assignment relied on GC-MS library matching rather than the study's target-standard co-injection subset. Teflon represents an inert-wall laboratory control, not a proposed natural material. Natural gas replenishment, electrical exposure, and product retention remain extrapolations.
suggestions: Attach the reported pH of approximately 8.7, 0.05 M NH4Cl, gas partial pressures, approximately 30-kV discharge, and 14-day protocol with approximately seven energized days.
Confirm histidine with an authentic standard and orthogonal analysis, and retain unresolved nitrogen provenance and hydrogen flux as explicit uncertainties.
Define a natural gas-water analogue without treating Teflon as a required environmental component.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The buffered borosilicate-contact protocol is supported as an empirical endpoint by Criado-Reyes et al. (2021). It does not establish a glass-catalyzed histidine mechanism, particularly because histidine was also reported without borosilicate. The principal limitations are target identification confidence and the unspecified correspondence between laboratory glass contact and a natural surface environment, not any inherent chemical incompatibility.
suggestions: Record the reported buffered discharge conditions and characterize glass composition, exposed area, and dissolved species.
Validate histidine against an authentic standard and distinguish any glass effect on histidine from effects on the broader product mixture.
Test a characterized natural surface analogue before transferring laboratory glass effects to a geochemical setting.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Criado-Reyes et al. (2021) support histidine detection in the buffered Teflon reactor containing borosilicate pieces. Representing this configuration as a protocol-level source term is appropriate. Neither a histidine-specific surface mechanism nor a molecular connection to the Shen intermediates was established. GC-MS assignment limitations and the environmental translation of controlled gas, buffer, and electrical exposure constrain confidence.
suggestions: Document buffered conditions, glass loading and surface area, discharge exposure, and product recovery for this specific configuration.
Use authentic-standard confirmation and time-resolved sampling to identify when histidine or its hydrolysable precursors appear.
Preserve the distinction between an experimental configuration and a demonstrated molecular mechanism.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The initially alkaline, unbuffered Teflon protocol has reported histidine endpoint support in Criado-Reyes et al. (2021). The network correctly avoids requiring a mineral catalyst. Initial pH near 11.1 must not be interpreted as a maintained pH throughout discharge and aging. Target identification remains less secure than in the Shen synthesis, and laboratory exposure does not establish a natural production rate.
suggestions: Document the pH trajectory and distinguish energized exposure, aqueous aging, and analytical processing.
Confirm histidine using authentic-standard chromatography and orthogonal mass spectrometry.
Evaluate reduced-gas retention and replenishment in a natural analogue rather than assuming a persistently closed reactor.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This initially alkaline borosilicate protocol is supported as an endpoint experiment by Criado-Reyes et al. (2021). The empirical representation is appropriate, but glass contact does not resolve the histidine mechanism. Changing solution composition during alkaline glass exposure and unbuffered discharge should be documented rather than represented by a single fixed pH. The same target-identification limitation applies as to the other configurations.
suggestions: Record initial and evolving pH, glass exposure, dissolved elements, and electrical exposure.
Establish histidine identity with authentic-standard confirmation and appropriate blanks.
Assess any natural glass analogue experimentally without assuming that all silicate surfaces reproduce borosilicate behavior.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The unbuffered Teflon-plus-glass configuration has direct reported endpoint support in Criado-Reyes et al. (2021). Its inclusion is valid as a distinct experimental protocol, without implying an additional established synthesis mechanism. Confidence is limited by GC-MS-only target assignment, unspecified pH evolution, and the unvalidated scaling from controlled reactor exposure to natural gas-water systems.
suggestions: Attach configuration-specific glass loading, pH evolution, gas conditions, discharge schedule, and recovery information.
Confirm histidine independently and distinguish free histidine from any material converted during subsequent processing.
Use isotope tracing and time-resolved analysis before assigning molecular intermediates or nitrogen sources.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Jiang et al. (2014) provide comparatively strong endpoint support through amino-acid-standard LC-MS/MS analysis and the reported seven-day product inventory. No histidine-specific mechanism or absolute histidine yield is established in the supplied account. The experiment used heated water and repeated methane/ammonia replenishment after evacuation, so it cannot be treated as an unchanged closed natural pond. Hydrogen bookkeeping does not establish measured hydrogen production or consumption.
suggestions: Attach the reported seven-day exposure, 125 mL water at 80 C, and twice-daily methane/ammonia replenishment, without inventing gas ratios or missing parameters.
Obtain absolute histidine yields, procedural blanks, and independent target-focused replication.
Investigate intermediate formation and distinguish discharge chemistry from subsequent aqueous aging or processing.

evaluation.network_feedback: This is a connected, sufficiently populated, evidence-qualified network with consistent reaction references and a credible precursor-fed route to histidine. Under the supplied deterministic classifications, all 12 reactions are balanced or balanceable; no conservation violations are assigned. Explicit coefficients should be stored, but discharge projections must not be interpreted as measured product stoichiometries, hydrogen fluxes, or nitrogen provenance. The unparseable mol_010 InChI requires repair and structural validation; it does not itself invalidate the stated histidine formula. Literature alignment is strong: the network distinguishes the Shen mechanism, conditional sugar-supply extensions, and discharge endpoint observations while acknowledging major precursor and analytical limitations. References and verified operating conditions should nevertheless be attached to individual edges. Staging avoids forcing incompatible conditions to coexist, but physical transfer, concentration, pH adjustment, and intermediate survival remain insufficiently specified. P2 and P3 are not experimentally closed upstream routes, while discharge protocols remain legitimate empirical sources rather than resolved mechanisms. Confidence reflects these evidential and chemical limitations, not the number of protocols, shared molecules, or environments. Listed problematic reactions indicate conditional chemistry, missing implementation details, or analytical uncertainty rather than proven impossibility. Pathway approvals use the requested 0.8 threshold; the complete network is not approved because its overall confidence is below 0.9.
